newsitem.title: USA: TCI tells equipment vendors to hold off shipments.
newsitem.headline: TCI tells equipment vendors to hold off shipments.

text.p: Tele-Communications Inc., the nation's largest cable television operator, has told its major equipment suppliers to hold back shipments in a bid to better streamline its operations, the company said on Thursday.
A spokeswoman said that TCI, which saw its customer base decline in July and August, sent letters this month to 30 major vendors to suspend equipment shipments until further notice.
Spokeswoman LaRae Marsik described the move as one to get a better hold on spending, rather than because of cash flow problems at the company, which is based in Englewood, Colo.
She attributed the July and August decline in customers, which she did not quantify, to recent rate hikes and to the usual summer lull in the entertainment business.
TCI's stock, which has not been faring well, lost 37.5 cents to $11.75 in late afternoon trading -- just above its 52-week low of $11.3125.

The spokeswoman said that, following the usual summer lull, the company did see some increase in customer numbers in the first week of September. At the end of last year the company had 12.5 million customers.
